methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $15M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Atomic Semi is a Seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Sam Zeloof and Jim Keller that has raised $15M+. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 11 companies in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, comprising 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent.

A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient granularity within the same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier cohorts—while 11 same-sector peers exist, fewer than three datapoints met narrow filtering criteria. Instead, a stage-progression method was applied, using the $15M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement. This yields an implied valuation of $38M.

Given the methodological constraints, the analysis supports a valuation range of $32M to $43M, with a median of $38M. The primary uncertainty stems from reliance on a single applicable method; triangulation depth would improve materially with additional comparable transactions or disclosed valuations from adjacent-stage peers in specialized semiconductor subsectors. Founder pedigree and technical positioning merit qualitative consideration but do not alter the quantitative range derived from available data.
